steps.body: When a scatter plot's form is roughly linear, a single straight line can summarize the trend. This **line of best fit** runs through the middle of the cloud, staying as close as possible to all the dots at once.
Drag the line until it runs through the middle of the cloud. The red gaps are the leftovers — a good fit makes them as small as it can, above and below in balance.

widget.prompt: Fit a line to the points' trend.
widget.successFeedback: That line follows the trend — the leftover gaps are as small as they get, balanced above and below.
widget.slopeFeedback: The tilt is off. Raising or lowering this line won't help — it climbs at the wrong rate. Fix the slope first.
widget.offsetFeedback: The tilt is right, but the line sits too high or too low. Slide it onto the points with the intercept.

predict.prompt: The cloud climbs from about (1, 3) to (6, 10). The best-fit slope is closest to…

options.label: 1.4 — up 7 over 5 across
7 — the total rise
0 — clouds don't have slopes

predict.reveal: End to end the cloud rises 7 while running 5: slope ≈ 7/5 = 1.4 per unit. A fit line's slope is the cloud's average climb RATE — quoting 7 takes the rise and forgets the run.

cml.actionGoal: Fit and perturb a model while residual direction and overall association update together.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Move one point far from the cluster. How should the best-fit line and residual pattern respond?

explanation.prompt: What makes a line a useful fit?

options.label: It balances the overall residual pattern and captures the association without needing to hit every point.
options.feedback: Exactly. A best-fit model summarizes a trend; it is not interpolation through every observation.

options.label: It must pass through every data point exactly.
options.feedback: That describes a surface feature, not the mathematical relationship that must remain true. A best-fit model summarizes a trend; it is not interpolation through every observation.

widget.prompt: What is the job of a line of best fit on a scatter plot?

options.label: To summarize the overall trend with one straight line
options.feedback: Right — it captures the general direction of all the dots at once.

options.label: To pass exactly through every dot
options.feedback: Real data is scattered — the line can't hit every dot; it stays CLOSE to all of them.

options.label: To connect the dots in order
options.feedback: It's a single straight summary, not a dot-to-dot path.

options.label: To mark the biggest value
options.feedback: It summarizes the whole trend, not one extreme point.

steps.body: A good fit doesn't have to touch any dots. What matters is that the line sits in the **middle** of the cloud — roughly as many dots above it as below, each one not too far away. It's a summary, not a connect-the-dots.

explanationVariants: A line of best fit need not pass through any data point — it balances the whole cloud.
The best-fit line summarizes the trend; hitting individual dots isn't required.

widget.prompt: Must a line of best fit pass through at least one data point?

options.label: No — it just needs to sit close to the whole cloud
options.feedback: Right — it balances all the dots; touching one isn't required.

options.label: Yes — it must touch at least one dot
options.feedback: Not required — the line summarizes the trend and may pass between all the dots.

options.label: Yes — it must touch the first and last
options.feedback: It doesn't have to touch any specific dots — it balances the whole cloud.

options.label: Yes — it must touch the outlier
options.feedback: It should IGNORE outliers if anything — it balances the main cloud, touching no dot in particular.

widget.prompt: What makes a straight line a GOOD fit for a cloud of points?

panels.title: Close
panels.body: Every dot should be reasonably close to the line — no large gaps.

panels.title: Balanced
panels.body: Roughly as many dots sit above the line as below it — the line runs through the middle.

panels.title: Direction
panels.body: The line should follow the cloud's direction (rising for positive, falling for negative). Close + balanced + right direction = a good fit.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — close to all dots, balanced above and below, following the trend.

explanationVariants: For a positive association, the best-fit line should rise to the right, matching the cloud.
The line's direction must match the data's: rising for positive association.

widget.prompt: The dots show a positive association. Which way should the line of best fit slope?

options.label: Upward to the right
options.feedback: Right — a positive association means the line rises to the right.

options.label: Downward to the right
options.feedback: Downward matches a NEGATIVE association — a positive one rises to the right.

options.label: Flat and horizontal
options.feedback: A flat line shows no trend — a positive association needs an upward slope.

options.label: Straight up and down
options.feedback: A vertical line isn't a function of x — a positive trend slopes upward to the right.

explanationVariants: The line of best fit replaces the scattered cloud with a single simple summary of the relationship.
It turns many scattered dots into one straight-line model.

widget.prompt: Why summarize a scatter plot with a line of best fit?

options.label: It turns a scattered cloud into one simple trend you can use
options.feedback: Right — one line captures and lets you use the overall relationship.

options.label: It deletes the outliers from the data
options.feedback: Fitting a line doesn't delete data — it summarizes the trend across all of it.

options.label: It makes the association disappear
options.feedback: It DESCRIBES the association with a line — it doesn't remove it.

options.label: It counts the dots
options.feedback: Its purpose is to summarize the trend, not tally the points.

explanationVariants: A line hugging only the top dots leaves most points below it — not balanced, so a poor fit.
If nearly all dots sit on one side, the line isn't balanced — poor fit.

widget.prompt: A student draws a line that runs along the very top of the cloud, with almost every dot below it. Is this a good line of best fit?

options.label: No — it isn't balanced; most dots are on one side
options.feedback: Right — a good fit has dots balanced above and below, not almost all below.

options.label: Yes — it touches the highest dots
options.feedback: Touching the top dots isn't the goal — the line should run through the MIDDLE, balanced.

options.label: Yes — any straight line works
options.feedback: Not any line — a good fit must be close and balanced; this one leaves most dots below.

options.label: Yes — it has the right slope
options.feedback: Even with the right slope, sitting above nearly every dot means it's not balanced — a poor fit.

hints: A good fit runs through the middle of the cloud.
Check the balance: are dots split roughly evenly above and below?
Here almost every dot is below the line, so it's not balanced — a poor fit.

steps.body: A line of best fit summarizes a roughly linear cloud with one balanced straight line.
takeaways: It runs through the middle of the cloud, close to all dots.
It need not touch any dot — balance matters, not contact.
Its direction matches the association (rising or falling).

concept.body: A line of best fit summarizes a roughly linear scatter plot with one straight line through the middle of the cloud — close to all dots and balanced above and below. It need not touch any dot.

explanationVariants: A best-fit line runs through the middle of the cloud, not along its edge.
The line should balance dots above and below, through the center.

widget.prompt: Where should a line of best fit run relative to the cloud of dots?

options.label: Through the middle, balanced above and below
options.feedback: Right — it runs through the center of the cloud.

options.label: Along the very top edge
options.feedback: That leaves all dots below — it should run through the MIDDLE.

options.label: Below every dot
options.feedback: That's not balanced — the line belongs in the middle of the cloud.

options.label: Through only the first dot
options.feedback: It balances the WHOLE cloud, not one dot — through the middle.
